key_insight: Earthquaker-AI combines a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant with hands-on robotics to teach earthquake preparedness to primary school students. It shifts learning from only physical simulation to deeper cognitive and metacognitive understanding of safe actions during earthquakes.
problem_solved: Primary school earthquake education often lacks interactive, personalized support that helps students understand not just what to do, but why and when to act. This paper addresses the need for a more engaging, scalable, and conceptually rich learning framework.
method: Builds on the existing Earthquaker STEM robotics project and adds a conversational AI assistant.
Uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation to provide grounded, education-focused responses from relevant sources.
Includes rubric-based assessment to evaluate student understanding and preparedness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper shows how RAG can be used beyond general chatbots to support safety education in a trustworthy, curriculum-aligned way. It is a useful example of combining generative AI with robotics and assessment to create measurable learning experiences.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram showing robotics module + RAG chatbot + rubric assessment
Before/after flow illustrating mechanical simulation versus cognitive learning
Student journey infographic: question, AI response, action, assessment
Icons for earthquake safety, robot, AI assistant, and learning outcomes
paper_title: Earthquaker-AI: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework with Rubric-Based Assessment for Primary School Earthquake Education
paper_authors: Xanthi Kokkinou, Chaido Mizeli, Nafsika Koulaxidou, Marina Delianidi, Konstantinos Diamantaras
